questions.question: The student _____ every day to improve her skills.
questions.explanation: Singular subject ('student') takes a singular verb ('studies').

questions.question: The researchers _____ their data carefully before publishing.
questions.explanation: Plural subject ('researchers') takes a plural verb ('analyze').

questions.question: He _____ to the office by train every morning.
questions.explanation: Third-person singular subject ('He') takes 'goes' in the simple present tense.

questions.question: She _____ closely to the instructor during webinars.
questions.explanation: Third-person singular subject ('She') takes 'listens'.

questions.question: They _____ all project guidelines before submitting.
questions.explanation: Plural subject ('They') takes a plural verb ('review').

questions.question: The designer _____ modern interfaces for mobile devices.
questions.explanation: Singular subject ('designer') requires a singular verb ('creates').

questions.category: Forms of Be, Have, and Do
questions.question: She _____ ready to start her new role next week.
questions.explanation: Singular subject ('She') uses 'is'.

questions.category: Forms of Be, Have, and Do
questions.question: They _____ ready to present their project proposal.
questions.explanation: Plural subject ('They') uses 'are'.

questions.category: Forms of Be, Have, and Do
questions.question: He _____ a clear plan for expanding the business.
questions.explanation: Third-person singular subject ('He') takes 'has'.

questions.category: Forms of Be, Have, and Do
questions.question: We _____ several tasks to complete today.
questions.explanation: First-person plural subject ('We') takes 'have'.

questions.category: Forms of Be, Have, and Do
questions.question: The company _____ agree with the proposed terms.
questions.explanation: Singular noun ('company') takes 'doesn't'.

questions.category: Forms of Be, Have, and Do
questions.question: The consultants _____ agree on the budget timeline.
questions.explanation: Plural noun ('consultants') takes 'don't'.

questions.category: Forms of Be, Have, and Do
questions.question: I _____ agree with the decision made yesterday.
questions.explanation: The pronoun 'I' always uses 'do' / 'don't'.

questions.category: Forms of Be, Have, and Do
questions.question: You _____ need to re-submit the application form.
questions.explanation: The pronoun 'You' always takes 'do' / 'don't'.

questions.question: The manager, along with two assistants, _____ traveling tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'manager' (singular); 'along with...' is an extra phrase.

questions.question: The reports, including the executive summary, _____ submitted.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'reports' (plural); 'including...' is ignored.

questions.question: The color of the office walls _____ light blue.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'color' (singular), not 'walls'.

questions.question: The total cost of all the materials _____ exceeding our budget.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'cost' (singular), not 'materials'.

questions.question: The director, as well as her team members, _____ attending the meeting.
questions.explanation: Phrases like 'as well as...' do not change the singular subject 'director'.

questions.question: The updates in the new application _____ system stability.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'updates' (plural), so it requires 'improve'.

questions.question: The officer, together with the audit staff, _____ reviewing the records.
questions.explanation: The subject 'officer' is singular.

questions.question: Marie and Marc _____ their grandparents every weekend.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' form a plural subject.

questions.question: Bread and butter _____ his favorite morning snack.
questions.explanation: 'Bread and butter' refers to a single unit/idea.

questions.question: The founder and CEO _____ addressing the shareholders today.
questions.explanation: Both titles refer to the same individual, so the verb is singular.

questions.question: The founder and the CEO _____ entering the conference hall together.
questions.explanation: The repetition of 'the' indicates two distinct people, requiring 'are'.

questions.question: Market analysis and strategic planning _____ crucial for growth.
questions.explanation: Two separate concepts joined by 'and' form a plural subject.

questions.question: Either the teacher or the students _____ responsible for organizing the event.
questions.explanation: The subject closest to the verb ('students') is plural.

questions.question: Either the students or the teacher _____ responsible for the equipment.
questions.explanation: The subject closest to the verb ('teacher') is singular.

questions.question: Neither the books nor the article _____ useful for our report.
questions.explanation: The subject closest to the verb ('article') is singular.

questions.question: Neither the article nor the books _____ useful for our report.
questions.explanation: The subject closest to the verb ('books') is plural.

questions.question: Either the manager or his assistants _____ going to sign the contract.
questions.explanation: The closer subject ('assistants') is plural.

questions.question: Neither the supervisor nor the employees _____ about the schedule change.
questions.explanation: The closer subject ('employees') is plural.

questions.question: Everyone _____ an important role to play in this project.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is an indefinite pronoun and takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Nobody _____ the exact answer to that question.
questions.explanation: 'Nobody' is singular and takes 'knows'.

questions.question: Each of the participants _____ a certificate of completion.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is the subject and is singular.

questions.question: All of the water _____ gone from the storage tank.
questions.explanation: 'Water' is uncountable, making 'All of the water' singular.

questions.question: All of the students _____ present in the auditorium.
questions.explanation: 'Students' is plural, so 'All of the students' takes 'are'.

questions.question: Some of the information _____ outdated.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable, so 'Some' takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Some of the documents _____ missing from the folder.
questions.explanation: 'Documents' is plural, so 'Some' takes 'are'.

questions.question: Neither of the proposed solutions _____ satisfactory.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' as a pronoun takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Somebody _____ left a notebook on the desk.
questions.explanation: 'Somebody' is singular and takes 'has'.

questions.question: The team _____ its matches every season.
questions.explanation: In American English, collective nouns like 'team' acting as one unit take a singular verb.

questions.question: The committee _____ made its final decision.
questions.explanation: 'Committee' acting as a single entity takes 'has'.

questions.question: The board of directors _____ meeting in the main office.
questions.explanation: 'Board' is a singular collective noun.

questions.question: The staff _____ attending safety training today.
questions.explanation: 'Staff' as a unified group takes a singular verb.

questions.question: The family _____ planning a vacation together.
questions.explanation: 'Family' acting as a single unit takes 'is'.

questions.question: There _____ a technical problem with the server.
questions.explanation: The true subject is 'a technical problem' (singular).

questions.question: There _____ many reasons to invest in microfinance.
questions.explanation: The true subject is 'many reasons' (plural).

questions.question: Here _____ your requested document.
questions.explanation: The subject 'document' is singular.

questions.question: Here _____ the financial reports you asked for.
questions.explanation: The subject 'financial reports' is plural.

questions.question: There _____ several candidates waiting for an interview.
questions.explanation: The subject 'several candidates' is plural.

questions.question: The United Nations _____ holding a global conference next month.
questions.explanation: Organization names are singular even if they sound plural.

questions.question: Physics _____ required for all engineering students.
questions.explanation: Academic subjects ending in -s are singular.

questions.question: Ten dollars _____ enough to cover the lunch fee.
questions.explanation: Sums of money as a total amount take a singular verb.

questions.question: Five years _____ a long time to complete a degree.
questions.explanation: Periods of time treated as a single unit take a singular verb.

questions.question: Three kilometers _____ not far to walk on a pleasant morning.
questions.explanation: Distances treated as a single quantity take 'is'.

questions.question: 'Gulliver's Travels' _____ a classical satire written in 1726.
questions.explanation: Book titles are singular.

questions.question: Reading technical books _____ your vocabulary quickly.
questions.explanation: A gerund ('Reading') as a subject takes a singular verb.

questions.question: To travel abroad _____ careful budget planning.
questions.explanation: An infinitive phrase ('To travel abroad') takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Studying every day _____ students retain complex information.
questions.explanation: A gerund subject ('Studying every day') takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Analyzing project metrics _____ team efficiency.
questions.explanation: The gerund 'Analyzing' is a singular subject.

questions.question: She is one of the students who _____ hard every day.
questions.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'students' (plural), so 'study' is required.

questions.question: He is the only one of the students who _____ hard for the test.
questions.explanation: 'The only one' is singular, so 'who' refers to 'one' and takes 'studies'.

questions.question: On the wall _____ several posters about sustainable development.
questions.explanation: Inverted sentence structure: the real subject is 'several posters' (plural).

questions.question: On the wall _____ a large framed poster.
questions.explanation: Inverted sentence structure: the subject is 'a large framed poster' (singular).

questions.question: Every teacher and student _____ required to register online.
questions.explanation: When 'every' modifies compound subjects, the subject takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Each book and article _____ reviewed before publication.
questions.explanation: When 'each' precedes compound subjects, treat the subject as singular.

questions.question: Every employee and manager _____ a unique identification number.
questions.explanation: 'Every' before nouns makes the subject singular.

questions.question: The software engineer _____ clean code for web applications.
questions.explanation: Singular subject ('engineer') takes 'writes'.

questions.question: The box of old tools _____ kept in the garage.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'box' (singular), not 'tools'.

questions.question: Most of the research _____ completed last month.
questions.explanation: 'Research' is uncountable, so 'Most' takes 'was'.

questions.question: Most of the survey respondents _____ satisfied with the service.
questions.explanation: 'Respondents' is plural, so 'Most' takes 'were'.

questions.question: The audience _____ listening attentively to the keynote speaker.
questions.explanation: 'Audience' acting as a unified whole takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Twenty dollars _____ the price of admission.
questions.explanation: Monetary sum treated as a single quantity takes 'is'.

questions.question: Building reliable applications _____ consistency and effort.
questions.explanation: Gerund phrase ('Building reliable applications') takes 'requires'.
